sections.title: Form and habitat
sections.text: A clustering palm of Amazonian wetlands, often with several stems reaching about 20 m. Its pinnate fronds form a crown at the top of each stem.

sections.title: Fruit and uses
sections.text: The clusters bear globose dark purple to black fruits, about 1–2 cm across. Their pulp is eaten in drinks and foods; the terminal bud is also sold as palm heart.

sections.title: Edibility
sections.text: The fruit pulp and palm heart are documented foods. This does not apply to other parts of the plant.
